business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Physical Arbitrage of Grade A Refined Copper Cathodes

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia – United States Trade Promotion Agreement (2012), Chapter 10 (Investment)
Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments between Colombia and the United Kingdom (2010)
Bilateral Investment Treaty between Colombia and France (2014)

Double Taxation Agreement between Colombia and Mexico (2013)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (creación de la UIAF); Ley 1121 de 2006; Ley 2010 de 2019 (art. 22); Decreto 830 de 2021 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUB); Resolución SIC 6815 de 2022 (manual operativo del RUB); Decreto 1497 de 2022 (sujetos obligados no financieros). Also applicable: Circular Básica Jurídica de la Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (Part I, Título IV) and Circular Única de la Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (Resolución 5925 de 2017, as amended).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Existence and Legal Representation of each corporate shareholder (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal de la sociedad matriz)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry / registrar in the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for parties to the 1961 Apostille Convention) or Consular Legalization (for non-party jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) granted by the foreign shareholder(s) to the Colombian representative for incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of the grantor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization), accompanied by certified Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card and address proof of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office or competent civil authority in the origin country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy affixed with Hague Apostille (or consular legalization) when the underlying document is public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Incorporation instrument (documento privado de constitución / pacto social) of the S.A.S., with shareholder signatures authenticated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Colombian notary (Notaría) for in-country signature authentication; for foreign execution, competent authority in the jurisdiction of signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for foreign execution; notarization in Colombia for domestic signatures

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, legal representatives, and UBOs against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Colombia's domestic frozen asset measures issued by the Consejo de Seguridad Nacional (UIAF). Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are identified per Decree 830 de 2021 and UIAF guidelines; enhanced due diligence (EDD) applies to PEPs and FATF high-risk jurisdictions. Screening is required at onboarding, upon any ownership change, and annually. Suspicious transactions must be reported to the UIAF through the 'Reportes de Operaciones Sospechosas' (ROS) system within 5 calendar days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) – https://www.rues.org.co; jointly managed by Confecámaras and the local Cámara de Comercio
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be written in the Spanish/Latin alphabet. Foreign names must be transliterated into Latin characters and adapted to Spanish phonetic and orthographic conventions. Non-Roman scripts or ideographic characters are not accepted in the registered name. The name must include the corporate type 'S.A.S.' or 'SAS' and must not be identical, assimilated, or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or a well-known trademark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a reconsideration request with the same Cámara de Comercio within 10 business days of the rejection notice, attaching justification, alternative name options, and trademark search results. If reconsideration is denied, an appeal ('recurso de apelación') may be lodged before the Delegatura para Asuntos Económicos of the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio within 5 business days, pursuant to Ley 1437 de 2011 (Código de Procedimiento Administrativo). The applicant may also submit a fresh name-reservation request after correcting the identified incompatibility.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not accepted as the sole registered domicile. Law 1258 de 2008 and the Código de Comercio (Art. 110) require a real physical address ('domicilio real') in the applicable municipality. A leased office or a shared/coworking space with a demonstrable business presence may be accepted. For ISIC 4662 (wholesale of metals and metal ores), a verifiable commercial establishment or coordinated/logistics warehouse footprint is expected; a mere P.O. box or virtual address is insufficient and may be rejected by the Cámara de Comercio and DIAN.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high risk (approx. 45% probability in the first 24 months of operation) due to enhanced AML/CFT monitoring of wholesale metals traders. Unannounced inspections may be conducted jointly by DIAN, UIAF, and the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio to verify actual commercial operations, inventory arrangements, and compliance with the UBO registration obligation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed per-book statutory registration fee, approx. COP 140,000 total

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat fee for Stage 1 pre-incorporation scope at prevailing market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada); Código de Comercio Articles 110 to 115 on merchant registration; Decree 1074 of 2015 (Single Regulatory Decree) as amended; Article 98 of the Law 223 of 1995 for mercantile registration integration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social, e.g. Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá through the RUES / SIE Web portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución authenticated before a Notary Public; if real property is contributed, a public deed (Escritura Pública) is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an S.A.S.; the authorized, subscribed, and paid capital is freely set in the bylaws. At least one share must be subscribed and the payment terms for cash contributions are fixed in the bylaws. Non-cash contributions must be transferred or perfected at incorporation. No escrow or mandatory bank deposit is required by the Companies Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) the subscribers' subscription to the authorized share capital set out in the bylaws is accepted and ratified; (2) the registered office is fixed at the address indicated in the bylaws for statutory notifications; (3) [Name] is appointed sole legal representative and [Name] alternate legal representative with the powers stated in the bylaws; (4) the opening of the company's bank account is authorized, including signatory designations; and (5) the legal representative is instructed to complete the registry before the Chamber of Commerce, obtain the tax ID and RUT with the DIAN, and undertake any ancillary filing required for the company's formation and commencement of its copper cathode trading activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the intended registered domicile; online via RUES / SIE Web portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for a certificate of name availability for the proposed corporate name. Submit at least one, preferably three, alternative names. The Chamber verifies that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered enterprise. Upon positive verification, obtain the official name availability certificate for use in the incorporation document.
required_dossiers: Application form with proposed corporate names
Copy of shareholder identification document (cédula or passport)
Power of attorney if filing through an authorized representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is denied or conditioned, file a new name request with a modified distinctive name; the Chamber will issue a fresh certificate within one business day of the corrected filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the private incorporation document
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in the district of the registered office; for electronic incorporation, the Chamber's digital authentication channel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución containing the complete S.A.S. bylaws: corporate name, domicile, object including wholesale of non-ferrous metals (ISIC 4662), share classes, capital, representation, governance rules, and audit provisions. All founding shareholders must sign; signatures must be authenticated before a notary or by certified digital signature when using the online incorporation mechanism.
required_dossiers: Certificate of name availability
Draft bylaws including ISIC 4662 copper cathode wholesale activity clause
Copies of shareholder IDs and RUTs
Bank deposit certificate or valuation report for any in-kind capital contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary observes formal defects, correct the affected clauses and re-submit for authentication. For digital filing, amend the online form according to the Chamber's validation notes and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration with the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social; physical or virtual window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the authenticated incorporation document together with the mercantile registration forms. Pay the registration fee and any ancillary levy. The Chamber verifies the document, registers the company, issues the Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation, and legalizes the accounting and corporate books if requested at the same time.
required_dossiers: Authenticated Documento Privado de Constitución
Formulario de Matrícula Mercantil
Formulario de Registro Único Empresarial
RUT preliminary registration if already obtained
Certificate of name availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber raises an 'observación', the drafter must respond in writing inside the term set by the Chamber and attach corrected documents. Unresolved observations may require restarting the registration application after paying an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration with the DIAN and issuance of the NIT
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – Sede Electrónica.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Chamber registration, complete the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) through the DIAN transactional portal. Select the applicable income tax and VAT/responsibility regimes, record the main economic activity as wholesale of non-ferrous metals (associated with ISIC 4662 / CIIU 4662), and register any foreign trade or customs obligations if the company will directly import or export copper cathodes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of existence and legal representation from Chamber of Commerce
RUT preliminary registration or company NIT assignment
Legal representative identification and address proof
Corporate contact and electronic notification acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT is rejected or blocked, submit an RUT correction via the DIAN portal attaching the Chamber certificate and identification documents; DIAN must resolve the correction within the terms of Article 599 and related rules of the Tax Code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account, book legalization, and foreign trade enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank; Cámara de Comercio for book legalization; DIAN and VUCE for foreign trade enrollment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account appropriate for letters of credit and LME warrant transfer operations. Legalize accounting, corporate, and stock books at the Chamber of Commerce. If the company will act directly as importer/exporter of copper cathodes, enroll in the DIAN foreign trade registry and complete the Single Window for Foreign Trade (VUCE) procedure for the customs authorization required under the relevant customs regime.
required_dossiers: Certificate of existence and legal representation
RUT with foreign trade activity codes
Board resolution authorizing bank signatories
Chamber application for book legalization
Compliance declarations required by the bank's AML/KYC policy for metals trading
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank applies enhanced due diligence for metals trading, provide updated corporate ownership charts, final beneficial owner disclosure, source of funds, and contract references. If VUCE filing is queried, correct the tariff classification and submit the additional documentary evidence through the same window within the authority's stated term.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial manufacturing licensing board is engaged for ISIC 4662 wholesale of refined copper cathodes.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial operating or manufacturing license applies to this wholesale trading activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required for warehouse/office-based wholesale activity; no full EIA or environmental registration triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable in the absence of an industrial process; applicable municipal wastewater and solid-waste rules for commercial office premises apply under local environmental code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for an industrial facility. For the registered commercial office, obtain from the local fire department the occupancy/fire safety certificate required by the municipal and departmental risk management regulation, and comply with workplace health and safety requisites under Resolution 0312 of 2019 if employees are hired.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales de Colombia (DIAN) - www.dian.gov.co
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity appointing a legal representative in Colombia must apply for a NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) through the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) using the DIAN MUISCA online portal, submitting corporate charter, foreign tax domicile certificate, and the agent's power of attorney; non-resident entities may receive a provisional NIT for VAT and withholding tax compliance when no permanent establishment exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia has no US-style check-the-box election; the S.A.S. is automatically treated as a corporation. Available elective regimes include the Colombian Holding Company (CHC) regime for qualifying intra-group dividends, the international trading company regime for export income incentives, and accelerated depreciation or goodwill deductions under tax certainty rules, all subject to prior DIAN approval.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold applies to corporate entities; any legal person performing taxable sales, imports, or exports must register in the RUT as a VAT-responsible taxpayer. The 3,500 UVT simplified-regime threshold (approximately COP 169,050,000 for 2025) applies only to natural persons, not to S.A.S. corporate exporters.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All sales invoices must be issued as electronic factura electrónica authorised in real time by DIAN using CUDE/CUFE codes and digital stamping. Export invoices use special document codes with 4XX series via the DIAN web service/API; customs export declarations are cleared through the VUCE single window and MUISCA, with mandatory submission of XML content and barcode for cross-border cargo release.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical exports of Grade A copper cathodes from Colombian customs territory attract 0% VAT provided the seller is the registered exporter in the RUT, the goods are effectively shipped to a foreign destination under an approved export declaration, and the sale is actually performed to a non-resident party. Export services are also zero-rated if exclusively used abroad by a non-resident and meet the Article 406 E.T. export service criteria.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Customs Declaration (Declaración de Exportación - Form 440 / DEX)
Bill of Lading or other transport document evidencing physical departure
International Commercial Invoice issued by the exporter
Foreign purchase order or sales contract
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Liquidación de Divisas) or foreign exchange declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN conducts ex-post audits of zero-rated export claims. Unsustained or fraudulent claims trigger retroactive VAT recapture at 19%, a 100% penalty surcharge under Article 648 E.T., daily default interest under Article 635 E.T., and possible criminal prosecution for tax evasion under Article 288 E.T.; aggregate sanctions may exceed 200% of the claimed credit and lead to cancellation of the exporter RUT status.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia), exercising exchange-control authority under Law 9 of 1991 and Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83, with enforcement supervision jointly performed by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso is freely convertible for current-account transactions, including trade and normal profit/dividend remittances, subject only to routine foreign-exchange documentation and reporting. Capital-account inflows such as foreign direct investment and intercompany loans require registration with Banco de la República, but there is no general prior exchange-control license requirement. Profit remittance is permitted once corporate income-tax obligations are certified, the foreign investment is duly registered, and the remittance is executed through an authorized local financial intermediary; transfer-pricing documentation must support cross-border intercompany payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from copper cathodes must be repatriated and canalized through the Colombian foreign-exchange market within 12 months from the date of shipment, extendable by the Banco de la República on justified application. The mandatory channeling obligation covers 100% of the export value; conversion to Colombian pesos is the default discharge route, but the obligation is also satisfied by deposit into a foreign-currency account with an authorized local bank, by applying the proceeds to authorized external obligations, or by other expressly permitted channeling transactions. The exporter must submit a foreign-exchange declaration (Declaración de Cambio) through the authorized intermediary and maintain supporting transport, customs, and commercial documents for control by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Colombian peso and foreign-currency current accounts, plus FX hedging and documentary credit desk.
Corporate operational account with capital-escrow functionality and trade-finance facility integration.
Operational account and commercial foreign-currency account with access to authorized foreign-exchange market.
Operational account for COP clearing and outbound documentary letters of credit.
Escrow and trade-settlement account for structured commodity transactions and LME-related flows.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary treasury clearing. Offshore digital electronic money institutions and EMI bank-account providers are not authorized local foreign-exchange intermediaries and cannot perform the mandatory canalización of export proceeds under Colombian exchange-control law. They may serve only as auxiliary payment rails for non-COP expenses or as information channels, but all regulatory FX reporting, trade settlements, and dividend remittances must pass through a Banco de la República-authorized commercial bank or financial institution. Any use of an unregulated EMI for commodity payments should be expressly avoided because it will trigger enhanced AML scrutiny and may void the evidentiary trail for the underlying copper trade.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person board attendance is not universally required for a Colombian S.A.S.; most tier-one banks permit remote or video-linked onboarding when combined with certified incorporation documents, an apostilled power of attorney, and passport-grade identification of each director and beneficial owner. However, given the non-ferrous metals trading profile and the expectation of high transaction velocity, enhanced due diligence normally mandates at least one senior executive or the appointed legal representative to attend a physical or secure video interview at the bank's institutional desk, with the board resolution expressly granting authority to open the account, approve signatories, and execute FX instruments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commodity trader with recent incorporation and no clear operating history in metal wholesale arbitrage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the Certificado de Cámara de Comercio, audited or reviewed opening balance sheet, board resolution appointing officers, notarized statutory purpose confirming wholesale of non-ferrous copper cathodes, and executed master copper supply agreements with named LME-registered refineries or recognized international counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners or shareholders without an established Colombian banking record.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver passport copies, tax-residence certificates, international credit-reference letters, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements, a bank reference from the investor's home bank, and a notarized declaration of the ultimate beneficial owner for submission to the bank's AML/UIAF compliance unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected fast-moving flows involving third-party financing, prepayments, or intercompany settlement outside standard commodity documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present original purchase and sale agreements, LME warrant chain or warehouse receipts, commercial invoices with Incoterms, shipping and inspection certificates, proof of underlying commodity movement, and copies of any intercompany loan or financing agreement registered when required by the Banco de la República.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Products and payment jurisdictions classified as higher AML risk for metal trading.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a transaction flow mapping document showing each purchase, storage transfer, export declaration, and final payment beneficiary; include an annual PEP screening, improved counterparty due-diligence reports, and legal counsel confirmation that no sanctions-listed entity or embargoed jurisdiction participates in the transaction chain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection into the Colombian S.A.S. must be routed by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 through the investing bank's correspondent to the collecting Colombian authorized intermediary, identifying the beneficiary as the Colombian S.A.S. The remittance must reference 'Aporte de capital inversión directa' and the bank must submit the applicable foreign-exchange declaration for foreign investment registration. Prior to wiring, the company must register the foreign direct investment with Banco de la República using the standard foreign investment registration form and upload the corporate share-purchase agreement, the constitutional documents of the S.A.S., and an identity document for each subscribing shareholder. The compliance verification is completed when the local bank issues the official copy of the foreign-exchange declaration linked to the inward remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for the acquisition of copper cathodes on the commercial/wholesale model are cleared through (a) direct SWIFT MT103 payments from the Colombian account to the exporter's nominated bank for open-account purchases; (b) irrevocable documentary letters of credit opened by a local Colombian bank in favor of the foreign refiner or trading house, payable against presentation of commercial invoice, bill of lading, inspection certificate, and LME warrant or warehouse receipt; and (c) LME warrant transfer under LMEsmart, followed by payment through the clearing bank by MT103 or against an advised confirming bank. All such disbursements must be supported by the relevant import declaration, underlying commercial contract, and the bank's trade-finance compliance review, including screening of all vessels, freight forwarders, insurers, and ultimate receiving entities.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: COP/USD outright foreign-exchange forwards executed with an authorized Colombian bank, supported by real export or import exposure in the copper-cathode trade.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the COP/USD rate, entered into through authorized local banks or regulated broker-dealers with appropriate underlying trade documentation.
FX swaps (swaps cambiarios) involving simultaneous spot sale and future purchase of USD against COP, available for treasury liquidity management where a demonstrable commercial purpose exists.
Cross-currency swaps matching USD trade receivables with COP operating liabilities, subject to bank credit approval and Banco de la República reporting obligations.
Purchased FX options (calls and puts) on USD/COP with tenors aligned to the underlying physical copper settlement and LME warrant disposal cycles.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registration Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce) in the registered office jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of each calendar year; renewal covers the previous operating year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal after March 31 triggers an extemporaneous fine calculated by the Chamber of Commerce with monthly accrual; failure to renew for two consecutive years permits administrative cancellation of the mercantile registration and compulsory dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements Filing (Estados Financieros) for the Prior Fiscal Year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the corporate domicile (electronic submission); Superintendencia de Sociedades if the entity becomes subject to surveillance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval by the Annual Shareholders' Meeting by March 31; filing with the Chamber of Commerce within 30 days thereafter, generally by April 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing may subject the legal representatives to fines from Superintendencia de Sociedades, suspension of renewed mercantile registration, and restrictions on profit distribution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Report (Información de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales), electronic platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after each fiscal year-end, i.e., by March 31 of the following year, unless DIAN grants an express extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file timely or submission of inaccurate/incomplete information triggers a penalty of up to 2% of the taxpayer's net equity under Article 651 of the Colombian Tax Code.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Timely statutory audit (Revisor Fiscal) is mandatory under Commercial Code Article 200 where gross revenues or total assets exceed 5,000 minimum statutory wages (SMLMV), approximately USD 1.6 million in 2025, or where the entity is a parent, public-interest company, or has more than 20 employees at year-end; a wholesale copper cathode trading business under ISIC 4662 will generally exceed these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian Financial Information Standards (NIIF/IFRS) as enacted by Law 1314/2009 and Decree 2420/2015; large entities apply full IFRS, SMEs apply NIIF para PYMES.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: All transfers of shares must be endorsed and registered in the Register of Members before shareholder rights may be exercised; the company must annually declare its ultimate beneficial owners to DIAN, including any shareholding movements or confirmation that no changes occurred.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Shareholders (Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Registro de Junta Directiva)
Minute Book for Shareholders' and Board Meetings (Libro de Actas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 - 500 per year (registered address and local agent, if contracted)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 8,000 per year (external certified auditor fee, scope dependent on commodity transaction volume and AML review requirements)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday; deduction of 50% of productive fixed asset investments; 25% deduction for technological innovation and R&D; VAT discount on certain productive capital goods; no preferential rate for copper wholesale trading.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carryforward, limited to annual offset of 30% of taxable income under Law 2277/2022)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 210 – Annual Income Tax and Complementary Return for legal entities (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios), filed electronically through DIAN Muisca portal (www.dian.gov.co).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December, the deadline is set by DIAN based on the last digit of the taxpayer’s NIT; generally between 15 March and 15 May of the following fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Colombian SAS tax ID, legal name, trade name, tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Colombian SAS NIT only; do not consolidate foreign parent figures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 53 – Gross taxable revenues (ingresos brutos operacionales)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total LME warrant and documentary LC revenues from wholesale copper cathode sales, net of discounts, returns and allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all sales closed in Colombia and all export sales attributable to the Colombian SAS under Article 24 E.T.; report arm’s length price if counterparty is foreign related.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 62 – Costs of sales (costos de ventas)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Acquisition cost of Grade A copper cathodes, LME warrant transfer fees, warehousing, handling and direct logistics expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support with commercial invoices, BBC clearing statements, and insurance documents; no inflated transfer prices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: freight, insurance, bank charges, LME clearing fees, legal and professional fees, depreciation and amortization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses with valid invoices and demonstrate the underlying commercial purpose for payments to foreign related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after statutory add-backs and deductions, including transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure all payments to foreign group companies and beneficial owners are reflected as taxable income for the Colombian SAS without artificial shelter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 101 – Income tax payable (impuesto a cargo)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross CIT at 35% of taxable income, reduced by tax credits, ICA deduction and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that any foreign tax credit is allowed under Colombian law; otherwise report full 35% CIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 105 – Balance to pay or overpayment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final self-assessed tax due after withholdings and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Remit balance by the due date; attach proof of withholding on dividend remittances if a foreign parent distribution is made.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing fine of 5% of the tax due (subject to a minimum of 14 UVT if no tax is due), plus 1.5% monthly interest on unpaid taxes; issuance of a final demand escalates the fine to 10% of net income or 2,000 UVT, whichever is higher. Criminal prosecution for intentionally false returns may apply.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed to non-residents out of profits already subject to the 35% corporate income tax (effective combined CIT+WHT 41.5%). Dividends paid from exempt or non-taxable profits are subject to an additional 35% withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA benefits, the foreign shareholder must submit a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by its home tax authority, translated into Spanish, apostilled or legalized as required, to the Colombian SAS before payment. The payer must have an updated due diligence file establishing beneficial ownership and economic substance. If the treaty rate reduces withholding, the Colombian payer applies the reduced rate at source; if already over-withheld, the foreign recipient may file a refund claim before DIAN through Form 110 or the relevant refund mechanism.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding rate 33%; DTA rates generally 5%–15% depending on instrument. Interest: statutory withholding rate 15%; DTA rates generally 5%–10% for bank loans and similar debt. Payments to listed tax-haven jurisdictions do not qualify for treaty relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Transfer Pricing Return required when a taxpayer’s gross income or net worth exceeds 165,000 UVT (approximately COP 7.5 billion in 2024) or when cross-border related-party transactions exceed 45,000 UVT (approximately COP 2.0 billion). Master File is required when the multinational group’s consolidated turnover exceeds the threshold set under Decree 2120/2017 (generally above COP 24 billion).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not have a standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime comparable to UAE/Caribbean rules; however, the tax administration applies GAAR, substance-over-form and the doctrine of abuse of legal structures. For a copper wholesale SAS, the entity must demonstrate physical staff, tangible or intangible operational resources, active LME warrant trading decisions, and risk control. Otherwise DIAN may disregard the entity and recharacterize transactions, imposing 35% CIT plus 200% penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating gross proceeds from copper cathode resales, recording fictitious warehouse invoices, fabricating LME warrant transfers, or otherwise inflating costs to reduce taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine equal to 200% of the evaded tax (or 10,000 UVT, whichever is higher); disallowance of false deductions; criminal fraud conviction under Article 402 of the Colombian Criminal Code: imprisonment from 4 to 9 years and a fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives who approve false accounting may be personally and jointly liable for unpaid taxes and fines; travel bans, asset seizure and debarment from commercial activities may be ordered; prison sentence applies for criminal fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SAS as a brass-plate intermediary solely to pass LME copper warrants and profit margins to a foreign parent without any office, employees, local decision-making, or real logistics and treasury functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may apply GAAR and recharacterize the entire structure: additional 35% corporate income tax on undisclosed income, 200% penalty on differential adjustments, and administrative dissolution of the company for fraudulent use of the corporate form.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and controlling shareholders can be held personally liable under civil restitution if the corporate veil is pierced; Colombian courts may impose travel bans, asset seizure and disqualification from serving as director of any Colombian entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the Transfer Pricing Return, omitting Local File or Master File documentation, using flawed comparability for copper cathode resales, or artificially decreasing Colombia-source income through inflated costs from foreign related traders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of 10% of the value of improperly documented cross-border transactions or 3,000 UVT per missing TP document; tax adjustment at 35% CIT plus default interest and penalties up to 200% of the adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and tax manager are responsible for timely TP filing and substantiation; personal liability attaches to the extent they knowingly conceal intercompany transactions, with criminal penalties for fraudulent concealment (Article 403).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing LME warrant or documentary letter-of-credit proceeds connected with unlicensed mining, sanctions evasion, or politically exposed persons without implementing an AML/KYC risk-based program for this medium-risk copper trading activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 2,000 SMMLV for non-regulated entities under Colombian AML rules; asset forfeiture of the proceeds; criminal money laundering conviction under Article 323 of the Criminal Code: imprisonment from 8 to 20 years and fines up to 50,000 SMMLV.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and beneficial owners who disregard red flags face criminal liability as co-perpetrators or authors of money laundering; personal assets may be seized, travel bans imposed, and they may be barred from any commercial or financial activity in Colombia.
